explanation: You’ve got the key distinction: quotes give Python text directly; an unquoted name tells Python to look up that name’s current value. Reassignment changes what a later lookup of that name returns. One small correction: an undefined name raises NameError; None is itself a value, not the same as an undefined name. Your summary matches the concept, though it doesn’t yet explain reassignment in your own words.
diagnostic_question: Without quotes, what does Python look up? What changes when that name is reassigned?

pedagogy.evidence_need: Explain how reassignment changes the value returned by a later name lookup.
pedagogy.claim_basis: The name lookup, quoted text, reassignment, and undefined-name error distinction come from the approved excerpt; the learner’s statements are evidence of their current understanding.
